findings.claim: The Go declaration patterns match any indented line that starts with `var` or `const`, including function-local declarations such as `var err error`. A removed local `var err error` yields the removed name `err`, and no added line declares it again if the variable was deleted or renamed. T1 then runs `git grep -w -F` for a very common word, so the sweep fires on trivial commits. Every candidate then has to be answered by the sweeper. This follows S6 (b) literally, which says 'a `const` or `var` name' and does not exclude locals. The consequence is noise at the T6b3 call site, not wrong behavior in this diff. The test 'an indented declaration' pins indented `func`, not locals.

EncodePolisher accepts a reply of up to MaxReplyBytes (1 MiB), then `encodeFile` indents the file with two spaces (stored.go:73). DecodePolisher re-runs ParsePolisherFindings on the stored indented findings, which enforces the same 1 MiB limit again. A compact reply near the limit, for example a large evidence array of short strings, grows past 1 MiB when indented. It is stored successfully, and every later DecodePolisher then fails with ErrInvalidStored (wrapping ErrReplyTooLarge). The record would be unreadable after it was written. The case needs a near-1 MiB polisher reply, so it is unlikely.
